articles.title: Scottish Football Podcast - Style over substance? Scottish football’s defensive dilemma - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Leaky defences, the enigma of Kasper Høgh and can Pogcognoli get his system to work?
articles.body:
Radio Scotland , · 04 Nov 2026 , · 27 mins

Are Scottish Premiership teams becoming too open for their own good? Charlotte Cohen is joined by John Walker and Rory Loy to examine the defensive problems facing Hearts, Celtic, St Mirren and Kilmarnock, and ask whether style is being prioritised over results. The enigma of Kasper Høgh is it a question of quality, service or the system around him? Plus, with Sebastien Pocognoli naming his latest Scotland squad, do the players really suit his formation, where does Scott McTominay fit and who should lead the line?

articles.title: New strategy launched to transform Scottish women's football over 10 years
articles.summary: The strategy aims to double the number of registered female players in Scotland, while also quadrupling attendances and audiences for matches.
articles.body:
The Scottish FA and Scottish government have launched a new strategy aimed at transforming women's and girls' football over the next 10 years.

Project 2035, supported by £250,000 of government funding this year, aims to increase participation levels, strengthen pathways into the game and establish Scotland as a leading nation for women's football by 2035.

A new taskforce will oversee the delivery of the plan, involving the Scottish government, the SFA, Scottish Women's Football, the Scottish Women's Premier League, PFA Scotland, Sportscotland and Cosla.

The strategy aims to double the number of registered female players in Scotland, while also quadrupling attendances and audiences for matches.

The ambition is also to see regular qualification for major tournaments - something the Scotland women's team haven't achieved since reaching the World Cup in 2019.

Why Scottish football is struggling to produce young talent

Weir 25th in Ballon d'Or and joins Olid & Cuthbert in award shortlist

'Why wouldn't you want to be here?' - Andreatta urges Scotland support

SFA chief executive Ian Maxwell says the women's game would benefit from the exposure that comes from big events.

"We saw in the men's World Cup in the summer, the impact that had across the country and to be able to replicate that from a women's point of view, we can't underestimate the benefit that would bring."

First Minister John Swinney said the project will build on the growth already seen in the women's game in recent years.

"Football has the power to bring communities together, improve health and wellbeing, and inspire young people to achieve their potential," he said.

"Our ambition is simple: every girl in Scotland who wants to be part of football should have the opportunity to do so, whether as a player, coach, official, volunteer, supporter or leader."

The launch comes amid continued growth in women's football in Scotland, with participation, attendances and investment increasing across the professional and grassroots game.

However, those involved in the project acknowledge challenges remain around facilities, volunteer support, coaching pathways and retaining players within the sport.

The taskforce will be responsible for monitoring progress towards the strategy's targets over the next decade.

articles.title: Sunderland bottom of Premier League: Is Europe to blame for struggles?
articles.summary: Will qualifying for the Europa League end up costing Sunderland their place in the Premier League at the end of the season?
articles.body:
Dinamo Zagreb under the lights at the Stadium of Light on Bonfire Night.

These should be exciting times for Sunderland and their fans, who before this season had been starved of European football for more than half a century.

Instead there is a concern the club's Europa League campaign, which includes a trip to AC Milan in December, has become a hindrance after the team's poor domestic start to the season.

Last season's surprise Premier League package are rooted to the bottom of the table, with just one win and six defeats from nine games.

Will a game against the champions of Croatia on Thursday (20:00 GMT) serve as a welcome distraction before Sunday's visit of Chelsea ?

When Sunderland won at Stamford Bridge last season in their ninth game back after promotion, the Black Cats sat second in the table after an electrifying start.

After nine games this season, it is a very different story.

Questions are being asked about the long-term future of manager Regis le Bris - the man who masterminded Sunderland 's return to Europe for the first time in 53 years.

So after last season's impressive seventh-placed finish, why are Sunderland struggling this time round?

Following last Saturday's 3-1 defeat at Coventry City, captain Granit Xhaka questioned the team's "courage", weeks after France defender Nordi Mukiele claimed the side had become "arrogant".

BBC Sport understands Le Bris' job is not in immediate danger and he will be given more time to turn things around.

The Frenchman, in charge since July 2024, is Sunderland 's longest-serving manager since Steve Bruce, who was in charge between June 2009 and November 2011.

Le Bris has credit in the bank for winning promotion and then claiming a European spot.

This season he has managed to propel the Black Cats into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, where they face fellow Premier League strugglers Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park.

But how long will Sunderland 's hierarchy remain patient if the club, two points from safety, stay anchored in the bottom three?

"They ended last season quite well to get into Europe and that felt really historic," former Sunderland loan signing Nedum Onuoha told BBC Sport.

"But there was talk then that maybe he [Le Bris] wasn't quite the guy.

" Sunderland fans who probably had their doubts last season, I really doubt that they will be thinking he is the manager long term."

French football expert Julien Laurens added about former Lorient boss Le Bris: "This is not looking good.

"I look at Sunderland and I'm not seeing him find the solutions to turn things around. For me that is really worrying."

Sunderland's paradox - San Siro trip amid relegation battle

Sunderland , who were playing in League One as recently as 2022, were lauded as one of the stories of last season, after doing the double over Chelsea and fierce rivals Newcastle , as well as holding both Arsenal and Manchester City at home.

The numbers suggest repeated success was always going to be difficult.

Only relegated Burnley and Wolves had a lower Expected Goals difference - comparing the amount of good chances created to those chances created against them - than Sunderland last campaign.

How about that dreaded second-season syndrome then. Is it even a thing?

Last season Sunderland and Leeds became the 53rd and 54th promoted sides to survive in the Premier League.

Of the previous 52, only 11 were relegated the following season (21%). The vast majority of promoted teams that stay up do not suffer from second-season syndrome.

With three-quarters of the Premier League season to go, Sunderland will rightly argue there is plenty of time to save themselves.

Yet those heady days of 12 months ago must feel a long way off.

Two of Sunderland 's seven league goals this season have come from the penalty spot, while they have finished with 10 men in defeats by Arsenal (Reinildo Mandava sent off), Bournemouth (Kevin Danso sent off) and Coventry (Omar Alderete sent off).

Meanwhile, Sunderland have failed to score a first-half goal in seven of their nine league games.

"Having been promoted many will have believed Sunderland exceeded expectations by finishing in the European places last season," added Onuoha, who made 31 Premier League appearances for the club in 2010-11.

"This season it is five points from nine games with seven goals scored. That speaks for itself in some ways - especially when three of those seven goals came in one game [a 3-5 defeat at Manchester City ].

"It doesn't feel at the minute that things are heading in the right direction."

Where is it all going wrong for Sunderland?

Sunderland spent £161m on 15 new players after winning promotion to the Premier League in the summer of 2025.

This time round, just £60m was invested on five players.

Most fans, however, will have been delighted to keep hold of experienced captain Xhaka and forward Brian Brobbey, who scored seven league goals last season before going on to score three for the Netherlands at the World Cup.

Brobbey, who has signed a new contract until 2031, has yet to score since returning from a hamstring injury, while former Arsenal midfielder Xhaka was downbeat after last weekend's defeat at newly promoted Coventry .

"I don't know exactly what the problem is," said the Switzerland midfielder.

"Is it concentration? Is it other things? We are bottom of the league but in football you need to think positive and to show courage as well.

Carl Jenkinson, who was at Arsenal with Xhaka, told BBC Sport his former team-mate's remarks were "concerning".

"He seemed really deflated and that is very unlike Granit," added the former full-back, who made 41 Premier League appearances for the Gunners between 2011 and 2019.

Laurens said the form of Xhaka and Mukiele, who helped Sunderland towards 11 clean sheets in the top flight last season, had dipped significantly this season.

"They are the leaders and they are way below the levels they had," he added. "The first one to pay the price [for the team's poor form] is usually the manager."

For many, the reason for Sunderland 's current struggles appears obvious - the added demand of Europe.

Their first European campaign since 1973 means at least eight games in the Europa League. Unlike in the Premier League, Sunderland have started well in Europe, winning two and drawing one of their first three league phase matches.

"Europe is great," added Laurens. " Sunderland fans will be travelling to Milan, it's wonderful.

"It could be a distraction for the players - especially the ones who have never played in Europe before. It's less time to practise on the training pitch.

"You play Thursday-Sunday and that's a very different dynamic to what Sunderland had last season."

On Wednesday, Le Bris described Sunderland as having "growing pains" this season.

He added: "Is it unexpected? I would say no.

"We are experiencing probably the most demanding challenge Sunderland have ever faced - Premier League, Europa League, quarter-final in the Carabao Cup, FA Cup later.

"It's a new journey - not for everyone because many of our players experienced this situation before, but it's still a new group, one year together.

"I think we are still competitive. We trust our team, our level, but repeating performances is different, this is the new step."

Sunderland have lost two and drawn one of their three Premier League games after playing in Europe.

They could certainly do with beating Chelsea on Sunday after playing Dinamo Zagreb to lift the mood.

Otherwise it is going to be an unhappy international break for Sunderland and their passionate fanbase.

articles.title: La decisión más difícil de Roig: peligra el Villarreal de Íñigo
articles.standfirst: El equipo no arranca y la debacle ante el PSG provoca lógicas dudas en el proyecto de Iñigo que era la gran apuesta del club
articles.summary: El equipo no arranca y la debacle ante el PSG provoca lógicas dudas en el proyecto de Iñigo que era la gran apuesta del club
articles.body: El Villarreal se enfrenta a una de las situaciones más delicadas de su reciente historia y ante la toma de las decisiones más importantes, en una u en otra dirección, de cara al futuro más inmediato. La debacle ante el PSG ha puesto patas arriba a un equipo que ya venía tocado y generando serias dudas tras la reciente derrota liguera ante el Espanyol. Más allá de lo bochornoso de perder un partido por 0-6, las lamentables sensaciones ofrecidas, la tremenda ineptitud mostrada por momentos, fue incluso peor que sufrir la mayor como derrota como locales en la historia del club. Y eso, en el Villarreal, no se suele perdonar. Lo cierto es que la dirigencia amarilla se encuentra en el peor de los escenarios que quería verse cuando la pasada temporada tomó una decisión tan importante como el cambio en el banquillo. Una apuesta arriesgada que tomaron a sabiendas que podía ser impopular, dado que la no continuidad de Marcelino comportaba cerrar un era que había cumplido con creces los principales objetivos marcados. Y se hizo de forma muy meditada a sabiendas de la importancia de la misma. Y se acabó para apostar por el que todos consideraban que era uno de los técnicos con más futuro en el fútbol español: Iñigo Pérez. El navarro llegaba al Villarreal tras haber triunfado con un Rayo al que, sin apenas recursos, llevó a Europa y a disputar su primera final continental. Y todo ello con un estilo valiente que le llevó a plantar cara a equipos mucho más grandes y con una filosofía y ambición sobre el terreno de juego que en el Villarreal veían ideal para arrancar un nuevo proyecto a largo plazo. Prueba de esta confianza fue el contrato por tres temporadas que acabó firmando Iñigo. Pero muchas veces los proyectos sobre el papel son unos y las realidades sobre el terreno de juego acaban yendo por caminos muy diferentes. Tras un inicio titubeante y pese a experimentar una mejora semanas atrás, los últimos acontecimientos evidencian que el proyecto de Iñigo no arranca y que las sensaciones futbolísticas de las últimas semanas son, cuanto menos, preocupantes. Tras el varapalo ante el PSG y antes de su comparecencia pública, Iñigo se vio en la noche del martes las caras con la dirigencia amarilla para analizar lo sucedido. “Lo que me preocupa no es mi imagen ni mi futuro, sino el no responder a la confianza depositada en mí”, afirmaba minutos después. El domingo se mide la Getafe en una de esas situaciones que invitan a que la palabra “ultimátum” aparezca ya en los titulares. Y tras el partido llega un parón liguero antes de visitar al Barcelona. Un escenario poco halagüeño para cualquier técnico en entredicho. En este contexto inesperado, el Villarreal se enfrenta a una de sus decisiones más difíciles. Especialmente si el domingo el equipo no da señales de recuperación más allá del resultado. La más popular es la habitual en el fútbol, la más sencilla y visceral: un cambio en el banquillo, aunque ello signifique descabezar el proyecto por el que tanto se apostó meses atrás. La otra, y quizás la más valiente por impopular en tiempos de crisis, mantener la fe en la que era su apuesta a largo plazo. Y hacerlo siempre y cuando haya respuesta del técnico liderando una reacción, aunque los objetivos de la actual temporada queden en riesgo. En ese casi y a medio plazo, será tiempo de reestructurar una plantilla con algunos recursos que casen mejor con la filosofía futbolística del técnico. Como en su momento y durante dos veranos se hizo con Marcelino (más de 25 fichajes en dos temporadas). Pero para ello, Iñigo deberá ganarse esa confianza, como hizo el asturiano, a base de cambiar unos resultados que, hasta la fecha, no llegan.

articles.title: Fenerbahce v Liverpool: From Derby to Champions League - Archie Brown's journey to face Reds
articles.summary: Fenerbahce's Archie Brown on his unorthodox journey to Istanbul, the moment of madness against Galatasaray and what Liverpool can expect in Turkey on Wednesday evening.
articles.body:
For Archie Brown, playing for Fenerbahce against Liverpool in the Champions League on Wednesday will mark another step in the justification of his own "unorthodox" journey that began as a young boy in the Midlands.

Brown, 24, was born in Birmingham and started his youth career at West Brom before joining Derby, where he helped them to their only youth top-flight title.

He scored a hat-trick in a 5-2 win over an Arsenal U18s side that included Bukayo Saka in the final between the North and South division winners.

Yet come 2021, the Englishman was frustrated by a lack of first-team opportunities and left to join Lausanne Sport in Switzerland at the age of 19.

"I've had quite an unorthodox journey to get here. I won't say that was always the plan," Brown tells BBC Sport.

"It was a mixture of two things. I'd seen so many talented players stay on the fringes of the first-team, playing with the U21s and then by 22, 23, they have no real first-team experience.

"And they have to go down into the lower leagues or non-league to try and build their career up from there. I didn't want to fall victim to that.

"Secondly, I felt it was important to get out of my environment, to learn a new language, experience a new culture, to help me grow up and mature as a person," Brown adds.

The left-back - who also plays in central defence and midfield - joined Belgian side Gent in 2023, before moving to Fenerbahce in a £7m deal in 2025.

The Turkish Super Lig side may be struggling for form - they are sixth and nine points adrift of leaders Galatasaray after 10 games - but Brown is adamant that Andoni Iraola's Liverpool will face an almighty challenge at the 48,000-capacity Sukru Saracoglu Stadium.

The Reds have happy memories in Istanbul, winning the 2005 Champions League at the Ataturk Stadium, but have lost their past five games against Turkish sides in the city.

"There are not really any comparisons in English football. There are no stadiums that can replicate the atmosphere," says Brown.

"Sometimes it can be difficult trying to communicate with your team-mates because it's so loud and that's especially when the other team have the ball.

"The only thing I can say to people in England is to come watch a game if you have a chance because it's really special. There are no boring nights in Kadikoy."

The pressure of playing for one of Turkey's 'big three' in Istanbul is immense.

Last Monday, Brown lost his cool against Galatasaray and was sent off for his role in a post-match brawl. Galatasaray accused him of physically attacking captain Abdulkerim Bardakci and he was given a three-match ban. Bardacki was banned for two games.

"It was a unique one," says Brown, who credits his Christian faith for helping him through difficult moments in his career.

"I always try to show my passion on the pitch and those derbies are fiery so anything can happen and unfortunately it came out in that way. But that's not my character.

"Everyone who's seen a Fenerbahce against Galatasaray match knows how intense it is. It's not abnormal for Turkish football, but it's definitely a lesson I have to take.

"Ultimately I'm disappointed because I've got suspended and the most important thing I can do is to be there for my team-mates. It was my first red card and hopefully my last."

Brown, who namechecks Ashley Cole as one of his inspirations, has represented England at youth level and continues to dream of playing for the senior side.

He is something of a utility player, equally as comfortable going forward as he is defending.

"In the Galatasaray game I played centre-back but in Champions League games, I might be higher up and pop up in different positions," he says.

"The good thing about how we play is it gives me a lot of freedom, and I've had a lot of trust from the coaching staff to give the game whatever I feel like it needs.

"I like to play free and try to put smiles on the fans' faces."

That freedom was evident with the manner in which he scored Fenerbahce's first Champions League goal in 18 years during their draw against Roma this season.

On the eve of this game, Dirk Kuyt, the former Liverpool player who is now interim Fenerbahce boss, said it would be an exciting opportunity for his side to show Europe what they're capable of.

For Brown there is a similar excitement about the prospect of taking on the likes of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola, come Wednesday evening.

"I love it," he says. "You play football to play nights like this against players like these, so I'm excited for the challenge."

articles.title: Maciá hace historia como el debutante más joven del Villarreal en la Champions
articles.standfirst: El ilicitano supera a Yeremi Pino al debutar con 18 años y 63 días
articles.summary: El ilicitano supera a Yeremi Pino al debutar con 18 años y 63 días
articles.body: Nada positivo puede extraer el Villarreal de una noche negra como la vivida ante el PSG. Pero si alguien recordará con el tiempo ese partido con cierto cariño será Carlos Maciá, quien disputó sus primeros minutos en una competición con la que cualquier jugador sueña. Además los hizo para hacer historia en el club gracias a su precocidad El canterano sigue creciendo a pasos agigantados y haciendo historia en el Villarreal. Con apenas 18 años y 63 días, se ha convertido en el futbolista más joven en debutar con el conjunto amarillo en la UEFA Champions League. Aunque , desgraciadamente para él, lo hiciera en un partido que quedará en la memoria del Villarreal como una de sus peores derrotas El centrocampista de Elche bate un récord que permanecía vigente desde septiembre de 2021. Hasta ahora, el jugador más joven en estrenarse con el Villarreal en la Champions era Yeremy Pino, que lo hizo con 18 años y 329 días en un encuentro frente a la Atalanta en la temporada 21/22. Ahora rebaja esa marca en 266 días, confirmando la importante apuesta que el club de La Plana ha efectuado por él esta temporada La historia de Maciá en el Villarreal ha ido creciendo a una velocidad de vértigo. Su primera oportunidad con el primer equipo llegó en diciembre de 2025, cuando Marcelino le dio entrada ante el Getafe con 17 años, tres meses y seis días. Ya en entonces, y siendo juvenil, destacaba en el filial de David Albelda como joven líder en el centro del campo. El Villarreal demostró su confianza ampliando su contrato hasta junio de 2031. Internacional con las categorías inferiores de España, Maciá es ya una realidad en el Villarreal y aspira a seguir escribiendo nuevas páginas.

articles.title: Vitinha, Neves y Fabián Ruiz postulan a mejor centro del campo de la historia: "No tienen equivalentes"
articles.standfirst: Vitinha, Neves y Fabián Ruiz sostienen en el centro del campo al PSG de Luis Enrique, que está haciendo historia en la Champions League
articles.summary: Vitinha, Neves y Fabián Ruiz sostienen en el centro del campo al PSG de Luis Enrique, que está haciendo historia en la Champions League
articles.body: ¿Forman Vitinha, Rubén Neves y Fabián Ruiz, el tridente de Luis Enrique en el medio del PSG, el mejor centro del campo de la historia del fútbol? Esta es la pregunta que se hicieron en el programa 'After Foot' de RMC Sport tras el 0-6 del PSG ante el Villarreal en Champions League. El trío formado por Vitinha, Rubén Neves y Fabián Ruiz no solo es responsable de la mitad de los goles del PSG, sino que, sobre todo, marca el ritmo de la "insolente superioridad colectiva del PSG". "Al evaluar un partido del PSG, es obligatorio empezar por los tres del mediocampo. Son ellos quienes hacen que todo el partido parezca fácil. Si añades jugadores excepcionales como Doué o Hakimi, ves que, al entrar en juego, potencian a todos los que los rodean. De hecho, cuando cuentas con futbolistas así —auténticos pilares que son los mejores del mundo en sus respectivas posiciones—, puedes dar entrada a jóvenes, hacer rotaciones o alinear suplentes en otras demarcaciones. No tienen equivalentes en el mundo y, de hecho, creo que en la historia del fútbol —si logran mantener este nivel de rendimiento durante tanto tiempo— no habrá muchos como ellos", apuntó el periodista Jean-Louis Tourre. Otros tridentes que podrían competir con el de Vitinha, Rubén Neves y Fabián Ruiz en el PSG podría ser los de Xavi, Busquets e Iniesta en el Barcelona, el de Gennaro Gattuso, Rui Costa, Andrea Pirlo o Clarence Seedorf en el Milan, el de Paul Scholes, Roy Keane y Ryan Giggs en el Manchester United o el de Casemiro, Toni Kroos y Luka Modric en el Real Madrid.

articles.title: Las dos caras de la Roma en Champions: del 3-1 al 3-4 ante el Real Madrid y del 0-2 al 3-2 ante el Manchester United
articles.standfirst: Los de Gasperini han perdido ocho puntos tras ser remontados o empatados esta temporada en Liga de Campeones
articles.summary: Los de Gasperini han perdido ocho puntos tras ser remontados o empatados esta temporada en Liga de Campeones
articles.body: Si los partidos duraran 55-60 minutos, la Roma de Gian Piero Gasperini sería uno de los mejores equipos de esta Champions League. 'La Loba' se fue ganando 0-1 ante el Fenerbahçe, 3-1 ante el Real Madrid y 0-2 sobre el Manchester United en Old Trafford... pero tras cuatro jornadas, apenas son cuatro puntos el bagaje que suman los italianos. Anoche, en Mánchester, la Roma vivió un nuevo capítulo de mala gestión del resultado. El equipo capitalino, que está viviendo una grandísima temporada en Italia, cedió un 0-2 a favor tras una primera parte de ensueño donde provocó el colapso del Manchester United y la enésima protesta de sus aficionados... que lanzaron pelotas de goma al campo tras el segundo gol romano. Por primera vez en la historia, un equipo visitante se colocaba 0-2 en Old Trafford en competición europea tras apenas 18 minutos. La Roma lo hizo... y aun así acabó viendo como, otra vez, les remontaban. "Creo que fue un partido diferente. Ante el Real Madrid todo se decidió en los últimos ocho minutos a balón parado, y no hubo señales tan claras como hoy, sobre todo después del penalti, que sin duda les dio impulso, y nosotros no pudimos mantenerlo", analizaba Gasperini desde Old Trafford. La segunda parte fue, claramente, mancuniana. Pero fue el penalti del 1-2 sobre Cunha (que tuvo que repetirse por invasión de campo tras la parada inicial de Vásquez a Bruno Fernandes) el detonante de la remontada. La acción, muy protestada por los jugadores de la Roma, dejaba dudas... pero Gil Manzano señaló la pena máxima. A partir de ahí, la Roma no pudo salir prácticamente de su campo y Cunha acabó siendo el heróe con un doblete en tres minutos. El cambio de Rodrigo Mora por Pisilli, sacando al mediapunta luso al descanso, fue un paso atrás de Gasperini que tampoco ayudó. "En este caso, esta noche, no tuvimos la fuerza para contrarrestar a sus atacantes en la segunda parte. Y luego, hay que decirlo, su primer gol llegó de penalti, y después hubo un error en el segundo, cuando el partido había recuperado cierto equilibrio", comentaba Gasperini, señalando el error de Balerdi en el empate. A la Roma, ahora, se le pone la 'fase liga' de esta Liga de Campeones cuesta arriba. Suman cuatro puntos de 12 posibles a falta de cuatro jornadas... y el calendario restante es duro. Solamente han ganado al Slovan Bratislava (4-0) y les queda visitar al PSG, recibir al Sporting CP, ir a Atenas para medirse al AEK y acabar recibiendo al Lille. Los de 'Gasp' necesitarán, al menos, dos triunfos para asegurar el billete a la siguiente ronda en su retorno a la Champions tras siete años ausentes.

articles.title: JJ Gabriel transfer news: Real Madrid confident of signing Manchester United forward
articles.summary: Real Madrid are confident of winning the race to sign Manchester United forward JJ Gabriel after reaching a verbal agreement with the teenager.
articles.body:
Real Madrid are confident of winning the race to sign Manchester United forward JJ Gabriel after reaching a verbal agreement with the teenager.

The 16-year-old is registered at United, but has not been back to the club since walking out in September.

Gabriel, who played against Atletico Madrid on United's pre-season tour, had been expected to become the club's youngest debutant in September's Carabao Cup tie against Brighton.

However, he has opted to look elsewhere for senior football and has been training on his own in Spain.

His availability alerted clubs around Europe, including Barcelona and Paris St-Germain, but Real now expect to sign the youngster in January.

Though no club-to-club talks have been held, sources have told BBC Sport Real have verbally agreed a deal with Gabriel and his representatives.

Gabriel, who scored a hat-trick on his Uefa Youth League debut, has secured a European Union passport, which is expected to make it easier for him to sign for a club outside England.

United would be due compensation should Gabriel leave, although the figure will be lower if he signs for a club outside the Premier League.

He was named the Premier League's Under-18 player of the season last term, despite being only 14 when the season campaign.

"The best 15-year-old in Europe," was how Gabriel was described by a United source this year, while former interim manager Darren Fletcher said: "The world is his oyster."

Speaking after the EFL Cup defeat by Brighton, United head coach Michael Carrick said: "We've got to be really careful of the whole situation.

"He's a young boy...from a club point of view, looking after our younger players - their welfare, their well-being, their exposure - we've got to be really conscious of that in this situation."

articles.title: Scott Parker: West Ham United confirm ex-midfielder as head coach
articles.summary: West Ham confirm the appointment of former midfielder Scott Parker as their head coach on a two-and-a-half-year deal.
articles.body:
West Ham United have confirmed the appointment of former midfielder Scott Parker as their new head coach on a two-and-a-half-year contract.

The 46-year-old replaces Nuno Espirito Santo, who was sacked on Tuesday after the club's disappointing start to the Championship season.

Parker previously led Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley to promotion from the Championship, but has been out of work since leaving the Clarets in April after their relegation from the Premier League.

He will take charge of the team for the first time on Wednesday when West Ham travel to Cardiff City in the Championship.

West Ham approach Parker after sacking boss Nuno

Green backs 'proven' Parker for Hammers job

Pragmatic Parker or a top flight contender?

First-team coaches Steve Potts, Gerard Prenderville and Billy Lepine will assist Parker while his former team-mate Mark Noble will also work closely with him in his role as sporting director.

The club will also make further announcements on the backroom team in the coming days and weeks.

"It is a very proud moment for me to step into this role and return to a club that means so much to me and my family," Parker told the club website. , external

"There was a warmth, a love, a feeling that I probably didn't have anywhere else. There was something which stood out constantly and that was the relationship that I built up with the fanbase here. That rapport and respect, that I felt instantly.

"More than anything, this is an opportunity that I am very excited about. I feel privileged and honoured to be the guy that wants to lead us back to the Premier League and be the head coach of this football club at this moment in time.

"My energy levels, my enthusiasm, my desire, my passion - it's absolutely running through and that's the feeling I had as soon as there was a conversation that this was possible. That's exactly why I'm here and why I want to be here."

'I've got out of this division three times'

Parker quickly became the front-runner for the job after the sacking of Nuno, which followed back-to-back home defeats by Southampton and West Bromwich Albion.

He becomes West Ham's fourth permanent manager since David Moyes left London Stadium in May 2024, and joins with the pre-season promotion favourites sitting eighth in the Championship table, six points behind leaders Middlesbrough.

"From my first calls with Karim [Virani, interim chief executive] and Daniel [Kretinsky, largest shareholder], it was clear they have a shared vision and desire to return the club to the Premier League as quickly as possible. I share that ambition and I'm very confident we can achieve it," he added.

"I've been in this division three times and I've got out of this division three times. This is a tough division, there is absolutely no denying it.

"I will use every ounce of my experience, every ounce of my knowledge, to have an understanding of what we're going to need to bring consistency."

He joins a club that has had a stuttering start to life in the Championship after relegation last season.

They have won two of their past six games and have lost back-to-back home matches - going down 3-2 to Southampton and then 3-1 to West Brom on Saturday - losses that have seen them drop down from second place.

The departures of players including Mateus Fernandes, Crysencio Summerville, El Hadji Malick Diouf, James Ward-Prowse and Freddie Potts secured the club about £150m in transfer revenue over the summer following their relegation.

They used some of that cash to pay Celtic a Championship record £22m for midfielder Arne Engels and spent a reported £12m on Norwegian winger Edvin Austbo.

Experienced campaigners Joel Veltman and Manor Solomon also joined on free transfers from Brighton and Tottenham respectively while they kept key players such as England winger Jarrod Bowen, Czech midfielder Tomas Soucek and Greek defender Konstantinos Mavropanos.

It is a squad that Parker needs to galvanise if the 2023 Uefa Europa Conference League winners are to return to the top flight at the first time of asking.

"He is someone who is held in high regard at West Ham United and throughout the game, and he was the unanimous choice of the board to become our new head coach," Virani said.

"He has fantastic experience and pedigree across an outstanding playing and coaching career, a clear and proven track record of success as a head coach in the EFL Championship, and a deep understanding of West Ham United, its identity and our loyal and passionate fanbase.

"We believe that all of these factors together make him the right man to lead us forward and help the club to achieve our objectives this season and beyond.

"Scott has the complete support of everyone here and, from the conversations we have had with him already, we believe he will represent West Ham United and our supporters in a way that we can all be extremely proud of."

Can Parker get West Ham back to the Premier League and keep them there?

Parker's managerial career to date has seen three promotions followed by much leaner times in the Premier League.

His first taste of senior management was at Fulham, who he immediately guided back to the Premier League with a play-off final win over Brentford in 2020.

Parker could not keep them up again the following season and left by mutual consent in June 2021. He then became manager of Bournemouth and led them to promotion as runners-up, ironically behind Fulham.

A few weeks into the new Premier League season, the Cherries lost 9-0 at Liverpool and Parker departed three days later.

He briefly managed Belgian side Club Brugge in the 2022-23 season before replacing the Bayern Munich-bound Vincent Kompany as Burnley boss in 2024.

Parker guided the Clarets to the Premier League at the first attempt, with one of the best defensive records in English football history and a 31-match unbeaten streak.

However, he could not keep the team up last season and he departed Turf Moor after their relegation was confirmed.

Parker is highly regarded at West Ham from his four years as a player at the club.

Having emerged at Charlton Athletic, and endured an unsuccessful move to Chelsea in 2004, he joined the Hammers from Newcastle United in June 2007, for a fee of £7m.

Parker went on to make 129 appearances in claret and blue, scoring 12 goals. He also won the club's player of the year award three seasons in a row.

In 2010-11, despite the Hammers' relegation from the Premier League, Parker also won the Football Writers' Association footballer of the year award and was nominated for the Professional Footballers' Association player of the year.

He started the first four Championship matches of West Ham's 2011–12 campaign, but handed in a transfer request after a bid came in from Tottenham Hotspur.

Parker completed a move to Spurs in order to further his England career, and he went on to be part of Roy Hodgson's Euro 2012 squad.

He later played for Fulham, before retiring in June 2017.

Why was this move not made in the summer? - analysis

As soon as the news broke that Nuno Espirito Santo had been relieved of his duties at West Ham it became clear that the club had identified Scott Parker as the coach they believed could lead them back to the Premier league at the first time of asking.

The only nagging question for me was why this move was not made in the summer giving Parker time to build a squad he would want and have pre-season to prepare them.

Parker's pedigree of guiding clubs to promotion from the second tier in his first full year in charge is unquestionable having done it at Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley. These achievements were at clubs where there was an expectation of success so the fact that West Ham have the same aim this season will not faze him.

He follows in the footsteps of the great Billy Bonds, the only other former captain to go on and manage West Ham. Bonds was also charged with gaining promotion, something he achieved.

There is no doubt where the issues have been for West Ham so far this season, starting games slowly, conceding first and on a number of occasions conceding too many.

Parker will bring structure and clarity to the team, providing a stable platform from which the front line can start exploiting their talents. He will want to quickly create an identity and will leave players in no doubt that hard work and commitment lead to positive outcomes.

The question of 'style' had been on the lips of a number of people in regards to Parker and much was made of Burnley's incredible parsimony during their promotion to the Premier League under him, but they were also the third highest scorers and gained 100 points, which is no mean feat.

He has players at his disposal to be effective going forward, and the coaching ability to make a rather leaky side more watertight.

The fans and the club will hope that is the perfect formula.

articles.title: Joan García logra la hazaña más buscada por el Barça en la Champions League
articles.standfirst: Deja, al fin, la meta a cero, tras 18 encuentros encajando goles
articles.summary: Deja, al fin, la meta a cero, tras 18 encuentros encajando goles
articles.body: Le ha costado. Pero lo ha logrado. El Barça, al fin, dejó su meta a cero en un partido de Champions League. Era uno de los objetivos más perseguidos por Hansi Flick y por todo el vestuario culé, y ayer martes, contra el Aston Villa, los azulgranas lo lograron. El conjunto culé se quitó un gran peso de encima que arrastraba desde hacía más de un año y medio. Todos ven ahora más cerca la posibilidad de conquistar el trofeo continental. El Barcelona volvió a dejar su portería en cero en la Champions League después de ¡18 partidos! consecutivos encajando tantos. El equipo de Hansi Flick consiguió poner fin, ayer martes en el Spotify Camp Nou, a esa larga y penitente racha con un firme 3-0 contra el Aston Villa de Unai Emery. El último compromiso en el que no habían encajado goles se remontaba al ya lejano 9 de abril de 2025, cuando los azulgranas se impusieron por 4-0 al Borussia Dortmund en el cruce de ida de los cuartos de final de la máxima competición continental. Desde entonces, el Barça había disputado 18 encuentros europeos y en todos recibió, al menos, un tanto del bloque rival. Borussia Dortmund, Inter (en dos ocasiones), Newcastle, PSG (en dos cruces), Olympiacos, Brujas, Chelsea, Eintracht Frankfurt, Slavia de Praga, Copenhague, Newcastle (en dos partidos), Atlético (en dos compromisos), Feyenoord y Galatasaray habían festejado una diana contra los culés. Hasta anoche. Joan García dejó su puerta a cero contra el Aston Villa, uno de los equipos, además, que más goles había marcado en las tres primeras jornadas de la Champions League: 12. El meta catalán fue uno de los protagonistas del encuentro contra el bloque de la Premier con paradas de gran mérito, sobre todo en la primera mitad, a acciones, especialmente, de Jackson y Manzambi. Se lució, pero ya lo hizo en otros cruces y acabó recogiendo el balón de dentro de su red. Pero ayer no lo hizo. Gracias a sus intervenciones y a todo el trabajo del equipo, como destacó Hansi Flick. "Era muy importante que hoy defendiéramos juntos, compactos. La última línea ha estado a un nivel increíble. También Joan García. Hemos defendido bien y estamos felices con lo que hemos visto en defensa. Todos los jugadores han dado lo máximo para terminar con la portería a cero", comentó, satisfecho, el preparador germano en la rueda de prensa posterior al encuentro contra el Aston Villa, correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de la fase de la liga de la Champions. Lograr dejar la meta a cero era fundamental para Flick, que considera la fortaleza defensiva determinante para lograr el objetivo de levantar esta temporada la Champions League.

articles.title: Chelsea Women: How Ellie Carpenter has become surprise star
articles.summary: Ellie Carpenter has become a surprise star for Chelsea this season after a strong start to the Women's Super League campaign.
articles.body:
When Chelsea were drawing with Roma at half-time and needed to find a goal from somewhere, Sonia Bompastor opted to bring on a defender instead of a striker.

Some of the head coach's staff questioned her decision - but Bompastor was proven right to trust Ellie Carpenter.

The Australian scored within six minutes as Chelsea went on to win 2-0 and has made a key impact for the Blues on several occasions this season.

"I made the final decision and someone in my technical staff said: 'But we need to score, and you are bringing on a defensive player?'" said Bompastor.

"We laughed after the game because I said: 'Right now, she's scoring a lot of goals, so I don't know if she's a more defensive or attacking player!'

"It worked so it's good. I was confident Ellie would create a lot in the second half."

So why has Carpenter been so effective for Chelsea this season?

Unbeaten Chelsea are top of the Women's Super League table, having only dropped points in their opening weekend draw with Aston Villa.

Carpenter has started all but one of their WSL matches and has netted four goals from a full-back or wing-back position.

In Sunday's 6-0 win at Charlton , Carpenter scored in the 13th minute, won the most tackles (three) and made the most ball recoveries (12) of any Chelsea player.

Only Khadija Shaw, Lauren Hemp and Victoria Pelova have had more touches in the opposition box than Carpenter's 56 this season.

And only Manchester City winger Hemp and Tottenham's Drew Spence have created more chances from open play in the WSL than Carpenter.

"She has been brilliant this season and she has that attacking prowess," former England striker Ellen White said on the Women's Football Weekly podcast .

"She has comfort behind her because she has trust in the other defenders and midfielders to give her the licence to go forward.

"I love her celebrations too! Opposition [teams] target players who are most prolific, but Chelsea have four or five who can score from anywhere on the pitch."

Carpenter arrived from Lyon in 2025 where she had worked with Chelsea boss Bompastor and won the Champions League together in 2022.

She was known to be an attacking full-back, like fellow Blues defender Lucy Bronze, and this season has become accustomed to the right wing-back position.

It has worked for Chelsea with Bronze moving inside as part of a back three and they have conceded just four goals this season, the fewest of any WSL side.

Carpenter's success at the other end of the pitch has been clear, but she has not reneged on her defensive duties - ranking second in the squad for successful tackles made.

Carpenter has always been a threat for Chelsea, but in her first season in the WSL a regular criticism was that she could be wasteful with her crosses.

That is something Bompastor thinks the 26-year-old has improved on and means she is contributing to more goals - scoring four and assisting one.

The Australian has also created 19 chances in the WSL this season and has played 141 successful passes in the final third, the most by any Chelsea player.

"Ellie is performing at a really good level. She has goals from her left foot too which is unusual," said Frenchwoman Bompastor.

"She is able to impact the game. The way we want to play as a team, she is really important out of possession and in possession.

"In possession, she always has the mindset and mentality to go forward. She has a lot of pace and is improving a lot in terms of her technical aspects.

"She is now able to deliver really good crosses, to be in the box and be clinical to score goals. I'm not sure she can have a bigger impact than what she is right now."

articles.title: Mac Allister: "La temporada pasada me hicieron saber que la idea era, por ahora, no renovarme..."
articles.standfirst: El argentino habló sobre su futuro
articles.summary: El argentino habló sobre su futuro
articles.body: Si nada cambia antes del 30 de junio de 2028, Alexis Mac Allister será agente libre en dos veranos. El internacional argentino, titular indiscutible en el centro del campo del Liverpool de Iraola, es consciente de ello... y habla sin tapujos sobre la incertidumbre que hay en torno a su futuro. Y aunque confiesa estar muy feliz en Anfield, no descarta nada. "Todo puede pasar antes de que me convierta en agente libre. Nos encontramos en una situación en la que me queda un año y medio de contrato, y en la que la temporada pasada me hicieron saber que la idea del club era no renovarme el contrato, al menos por ahora. Y bueno, obviamente fue una situación dolorosa", reconocía el propio Mac Allister en una entrevista con Gastón Edul. Una situación que, desde luego, sorprende... pues Mac Allister, de 27 años, ha sido una pieza importante en el Liverpool desde que llegó de Brighton allá por 2023. Los planes de Mac Allister, si dependieran únicamente de él, parecen claros: seguir. "Aún me me queda tiempo en este club, que es lo que más deseo: seguir aquí", confesaba. "Pero la realidad es que ha cambiado el entrenador, ha cambiado el director deportivo y están llegando nuevos inversores al club. Así que creo que hoy me encuentro en una situación en la que puede pasar cualquier cosa y, bueno, ya veremos qué depara el futuro. Soy feliz aquí", añadía.

articles.title: Aplazados el Granada-Tenerife y el Andorra-Mallorca tras el fallecimiento de De Miguel
articles.standfirst: Las nuevas fechas de ambos partidos serán anunciadas próximamente
articles.summary: La nueva fecha del partido será anunciada próximamente
articles.body: Ya es oficial lo que todo el mundo esperaba. El duelo que debía enfrentar al Granada con el Tenerife este sábado, 7 de noviembre, en Los Cármenes desde las 21:00 horas ha quedado aplazado tras la trágica pérdida de Jesús de Miguel. Igualmente, el choque entre Andorra y Mallorca tampoco se disputará este domingo a las 14:00 horas como estaba previsto por el mismo motivo. Las nuevas fechas de ambos partidos serán anunciadas próximamente. El fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel en la mañana de ayer en el hospital, provocado por un fuerte golpe con Jesús Owono durante la disputa del Tenerife-Andorra, ha llevado a LaLiga a aplazar ambos encuentros como habían solicitado los dos clubes implicados en el partido del lunes para respetar el luto de una plantilla y una afición tinerfeña que en estos momentos está rota de dolor. En la tarde de ayer ya suspendió la RFEF la jornada copera, en señal de respeto. Está por ver si finalmente no se juega toda la jornada o solamente el choque que involucra al conjunto canario. Tanto el Granada como el Mallorca no sólo han puesto de su parte, sino que han expresado su comprensión ante las circunstancias excepcionales que han motivado la decisión. En su comunicado, el Mallorca subraya que en estos momentos deben prevalecer “el respeto y la sensibilidad ante una situación de profundo dolor”.

articles.title: Wales: Craig Bellamy announces 26-man squad for UEFA Nations League matches against Norway and Portugal
articles.summary: Harry Wilson and Joe Rodon among those recalled to Wales squad by Craig Bellamy; the Dragons face two crucial UEFA Nations League matches - Norway in Oslo on November 14 and Portugal in Cardiff on November 17
articles.body:
The Dragons sit third in Group A4 after beating Norway during the previous international break, but also suffering two defeats to Denmark and one against Portugal.

On Saturday November 14, they face Norway in Oslo, before a sold-out clash with Portugal at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday November 17.

Leeds winger Wilson withdrew from the squad for the previous camp in September with a quadricep injury, while club team-mate Rodon has seemingly recovered from a hamstring injury suffered during the 1-1 draw with Brentford on August 30.

Elsewhere, Man Utd goalkeeper Karl Darlow also returns to the squad, while U21 stopper Joe Duncan earns his first senior call-up.

Cardiff's Rubin Colwill earns his first call-up since last November, while Kai Andrews - on loan at Oxford from Coventry - returns for the first time since June.

If Wales finish in the top two, they will progress to the quarter-finals, but if they finish third, they would face a relegation play-off against a team from League B. Both matches will take place in March.

Should they finish bottom of their group, they will either face a relegation play-off or direct relegation.

articles.title: Wales Nations League squad: Harry Wilson returns and Joe Duncan earns call
articles.summary: Harry Wilson is back in Wales' squad for their Nations League matches against Norway and Portugal, while goalkeeper Joe Duncan earns his first call.
articles.body:
Harry Wilson is back in Wales' squad for their Nations League matches against Norway and Portugal, while there is a first call-up for young goalkeeper Joe Duncan.

Wilson has been one of Wales' most influential players in recent years but injuries mean the Leeds United attacking midfielder has not featured for his country since March.

His Leeds team-mate, centre-back Joe Rodon, also returns despite not playing since injuring his hamstring in August.

"We've clearly seen in my time here the influence Harry's had," said Wales head coach Craig Bellamy. "He's had a big influence on the team. He's been outstanding for us.

"Joe's been immense, so it's great having him. Players have to come through [for their clubs] this week so, fingers crossed when we report Sunday, we have these players available because they're really important for us."

Cardiff City playmaker Rubin Colwill is recalled but fellow midfielder Jordan James is out after sustaining an injury while playing for Wolves against the Bluebirds last Saturday.

The only new call-up is 20-year-old Duncan, who is on loan at National League side Southend United from Championship outfit Bristol City, as Bellamy looks to freshen up Wales' ageing crop of keepers.

Born in Bristol but qualifying for Wales through his maternal grandfather from Cardiff, Duncan has represented Wales Under-21s and replaces Everton back-up Tom King in the senior squad.

Wales have a shortage of goalkeeping options, with a noticeable lack of young players emerging. First-team regulars Karl Darlow and Danny Ward are 36 and 33 respectively, while King is 31.

"It's a clear issue at this moment, of course it is, because of the age of our goalkeepers," said Bellamy.

"At one stage a long time ago, we had the world's number one goalkeeper [Neville Southall], most incredible goalkeeper.

"But this period now, where's the next one? One of my best friends is the manager at Southend [Kieron Dyer], who gives me big updates. He's been over the moon with him [Duncan].

"When I've seen him, I've been really happy with him. The National League will test you, it will test your toughness, there's no protection for goalkeepers, so I think it's a brilliant part of his development.

"The more you see him and you see him live then it makes it clear if we think he's going to be ready in the next couple of years. He might not be ready right now but we always have to have one eye on the future."

Wales, who are looking to preserve their place in the Nations League's top tier, face Norway in Oslo on Saturday, 14 November before finishing their campaign at home against Portugal the following Tuesday.

Wales are third in Group A4, with their only win from four matches so far coming against World Cup quarter-finalists Norway in Cardiff last month.

Bellamy's side could still finish in second, third or fourth place.

A top-two spot would take Wales to the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2027.

Finishing third would mean a relegation play-off against a League B team in March while finishing bottom of the group would result in either a relegation play-off or direct relegation, depending on the ranking with other League A groups.

articles.title: A qué hora es el AEK Atenas - Real Madrid: horario, canal y dónde ver en TV el partido de Champions League en directo hoy
articles.standfirst: Todos los detalles sobre el partido correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de la fase liga de la Champions League.
articles.summary: Todos los detalles sobre el partido correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de la fase liga de la Champions League.
articles.body: El Real Madrid visita Grecia con el objetivo de prolongar su pleno de victorias en la Champions League. El conjunto blanco, dirigido por José Mourinho, ha ganado sus tres primeros encuentros de la competición y quiere sumar otros tres puntos para acercarse a la clasificación directa para los octavos de final. El AEK, por su parte, afronta uno de los partidos más exigentes de su calendario europeo. El equipo griego intentará aprovechar el apoyo de su afición para sorprender al Real Madrid y conseguir una victoria que le permita mejorar su situación en la clasificación. El partido entre el AEK y el Real Madrid se juega hoy miércoles 4 de noviembre a las 18:45 horas (horario peninsular español). El encuentro comenzará a las 19:45 horas en Grecia. El partido entre el AEK y el Real Madrid, correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de la fase liga de la Champions League, se podrá ver por televisión en directo a través de Movistar Liga de Campeones, disponible en Movistar Plus+ y Orange TV. También se podrá seguir el encuentro a través de la narración de Radio MARCA y con los comentarios en directo de MARCA.com. Desde dos horas antes, sigue la previa y los onces de ambos equipos. Tras el encuentro, podrás leer la crónica, las declaraciones de los protagonistas y ver el resumen con las mejores jugadas y los goles. El AEK de Atenas llega al encuentro después de perder por 5-1 contra el Manchester City en la tercera jornada de la Champions League. El conjunto griego, que comenzó la competición con una victoria por 1-0 ante el LASK, también cayó por 3-1 frente al Shakhtar Donetsk. Actualmente ocupa la posición número 27 de la clasificación, con tres puntos. El Real Madrid visita Atenas después de ganar por 4-1 al Leipzig en la tercera jornada de la Champions League. El equipo blanco también se impuso al Inter de Milán (2-1) y a la Roma (3-4) en sus dos primeros encuentros europeos. Actualmente ocupa la quinta posición, con nueve puntos, y busca su cuarta victoria consecutiva en la competición.

articles.body: El Borussia Dortmund y el Real Betis se enfrentan en un partido correspondiente a la jornada 4 de la fase liga de la Champions League. El encuentro se disputa este miércoles 4 de noviembre a las 21.00 horas en el Signal Iduna Park de Dortmund. El conjunto alemán afronta una cita de máxima exigencia ante un Betis que llega con pleno de victorias y situado en la quinta posición de la clasificación, mientras que el equipo de Niko Kovac necesita sumar para acercarse a los puestos que dan acceso directo a octavos. El Dortmund llega al duelo europeo tras empatar 2-2 en Bayern de Múnich en la última jornada de Bundesliga y ocupa la segunda posición del campeonato alemán, invicto con 18 puntos tras ocho jornadas. En la Champions, los alemanes suman seis puntos: vencieron al Villarreal (3-2) y al Sabah (2-1), pero cayeron en Bodo/Glimt (1-0), por lo que no pueden permitirse otro tropiezo si quieren pelear por el top 8. Serhou Guirassy es su principal referencia ofensiva, con cuatro goles en los tres primeros partidos de la competición. El Betis aterriza en Dortmund en un momento histórico. El equipo de Manuel Pellegrini ha ganado sus tres encuentros en la fase liga. Los verdiblancos vienen además de ganar 2-1 al Málaga en LaLiga, donde son cuartos con 23 puntos, y llegan con la ilusión de una afición que se ha desplazado masivamente a la ciudad alemana. El duelo tendrá un componente especial: será el primer enfrentamiento oficial entre Borussia Dortmund y Real Betis en competición europea. El Betis buscará mantener su pleno ante un rival de mayor peso continental, mientras el Dortmund intentará aprovechar la intensidad de su estadio para frenar la mejor racha europea de su historia reciente. El partido entre el Borussia Dortmund y el Real Betis se juega el miércoles 4 de noviembre a las 21.00 horas (horario peninsular español) en el Signal Iduna Park. El choque corresponde a la cuarta jornada de la fase liga de la Champions League 2026-27. Desde varias horas antes del inicio se podrán consultar la última hora de ambos equipos, las alineaciones probables y todas las novedades de una cita clave para las aspiraciones europeas del Betis. Tras el partido, estarán disponibles la crónica, las declaraciones de los protagonistas, el análisis y el resumen con las mejores jugadas y los goles.

articles.title: Jesus de Miguel death: Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono 'would never intentionally hurt anyone' says team-mate
articles.summary: Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono "would never intentionally hurt anyone" and is "deeply affected" by the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel, his team-mate said on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Goalkeeper Jesus Owono "would never intentionally hurt anyone" and has been "deeply affected" by the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel, an FC Andorra team-mate said on Wednesday.

Tenerife player De Miguel, 30, died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

The world of football has paid tribute to De Miguel, a father-of-one who joined Tenerife in summer 2025, with a minute's silence being held at all European games this week.

Writing on social media, FC Andorra centre-back Lautaro Spatz said Owono was devastated.

He paid tribute to De Miguel but added: "I also want to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who is deeply affected by what has happened.

"Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.

"In football, unfortunate incidents can happen but no-one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences."

Players from Andorra held a minute's silence before a voluntary training session on Wednesday. Owono did not attend the session.

Football world mourns Tenerife striker De Miguel

Tenerife and Andorra were drawing 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred.

Owono ran towards the centre circle to clear a long ball when his knee appeared to collide with De Miguel.

The striker lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff treated him before he was taken by ambulance from Tenerife's Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez to hospital.

Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned.

The 25-year-old goalkeeper, who had over 30,000 followers on Instagram on Tuesday morning, has since deactivated his account.

Police in Spain opened a routine investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter following De Miguel's death.

Under Spanish law, any death that is deemed non-natural automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.

Owono has made 47 international appearances for Equatorial Guinea.

The president of Equatorial Guinea's football federation, Venancio Tomas Micha, issued a statement on Tuesday offering "all our human and professional backing" to the player.

"As the involuntary protagonist of this tragic incident in the game, he is living through this situation with deep sorrow and distress," he added.

On Tuesday, mourners laid flowers and lit candles beneath a black and white image of De Miguel at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.

Tenerife said in a statement they will commence six official days of mourning, with all club activities suspended during this time.

The club's players, staff and officials will attend De Miguel's funeral, which will take place in Navahermosa, Toledo.

Tenerife will also open their home ground on Saturday evening to allow supporters to "bid a fitting farewell".

"Jesus de Miguel's family would like to thank everyone for their messages of support and, from the bottom of their hearts, ask that their privacy be respected at this terrible time. May he rest in peace," added the club statement.

Tenerife and Andorra's Spanish second division matches scheduled for the weekend, against Granada and Mallorca respectively, have been postponed.

articles.standfirst: El ciclón luso del Monza deslumbra en la Serie A y ya lo han tasado en 50 millones
articles.summary: El ciclón luso del Monza deslumbra en la Serie A y ya lo han tasado en 50 millones
articles.body: Ha llegado a la Serie A como un torbellino. Gustavo Varela hace sonreír al Monza. Los goles del jovencísimo ariete portugués han llamado la atención en toda Europa. Con 21 años, Varela tiene a tiro la absoluta de Portugal, a la que puede acceder esta misma semana y su crecimiento en Italia está siendo exponencial. El Monza sabe que tiene que combinar su nivel deportivo, en él está basada media salvación, y su potencial en el mercado. Varios equipos de los grandes ya han movido ficha entorno al delantero y el Barcelona es el mejor colocado en España. El club catalán ha monitorizado al luso, un delantero que trabaja duro, como le gusta a Flick, pero al que los goles se le caen de los bolsillos, un futbolista total, joven y que encaja perfectamente en la dinámica del club blaugrana. Pero para Deco no va a ser sencillo. Hay varios equipos que ya han movido el árbol entorno al delantero. Según asegura A Bola, Napoli y Milan ya han tocado a la puerta del Monza para preguntar por el delantero. En la Premier el Arsenal ha hecho un movimientos y también está en la lista de refuerzos del Totenham y del Leipzig, en Alemania. El internacional sub 21 portugués, que está en todas las quinielas para dar el salto en esta convocatoria a la absoluta, empezó a despuntar en las categorías inferiores de Benfica. Llegó hasta el filial y de allí dio el salto. Primero fue cedido al Gil Vicente y este verano Benfica decidió traspasarlo al Monza por dos millones y medio de euros. En sus primeros nueve partidos oficiales en Italia, entre Liga y copa, Varela ha marcado nueve goles y se ha convertido en una de las sensaciones del campeonato. Hay que recordar que el Benfica se quedó un 20% de un futuro traspaso por lo que una venta millonaria del Monza les dejaría un buen pellizco en caja.

articles.title: ¡Rafa Nadal entrará en la Junta Directiva del Real Madrid!
articles.standfirst: Será propuesto en la Asamblea del día 21 de noviembre
articles.summary: Será propuesto en la Asamblea del día 21 de noviembre
articles.body: Rafa Nadal está a punto de convertirse en miembro de la Junta Directiva del Real Madrid. El club lo propondrá a sus socios en la Asamblea del día 21 de noviembre y en caso de ser aprobado, como se espera, se convertirá en miembro de la Junta del Madrid. Así lo ha comunicado el club blanco, que celebrará una Asamblea Extraordinaria para aprobar la entrada de la leyenda del tenis: "Propuesta de la Junta Directiva de ratificación por la Asamblea General Extraordinaria de D. Rafael Nadal Parera como miembro de la Junta Directiva del Real Madrid C. F., de acuerdo con el artículo 46 de los Estatutos Sociales. En relación con dicho Orden del Día, la Junta aprobó por unanimidad someter a la aprobación de la Asamblea General Extraordinaria la siguiente propuesta: Ratificar el nombramiento de D. Rafael Nadal Parera como miembro de la Junta Directiva del Real Madrid C. F., de acuerdo con el artículo 46 de los Estatutos Sociales". La Asamblea Ordinaria del Real Madrid se celebrará el día 21, a las 9.00 en primera convocatoria y a las 10.00 en segunda. En ella, se tratarán los temas habituales: Informe del presidente, examen y aprobación, en su caso, de la Liquidación del Presupuesto, la Memoria, el Balance de Situación y la Cuenta de Pérdidas y Ganancias del Club, así como las consolidadas con las empresas participadas, correspondientes al Ejercicio 2025/2026; examen y aprobación, en su caso, del Presupuesto Consolidado de Ingresos y Gastos y el Proyecto de Actividades para el Ejercicio 2026/2027; propuesta de cuotas sociales para la temporada 2027/2028 y ruegos y preguntas. Pero el bombazo llegará con la Asamblea Extraordinaria que empezará inmediatamente después, con un único punto del día: la entrada de Rafael Nadal como miembro de la Junta Directiva. Para el club blanco, es una de las más grandes leyendas de la historia del deporte y un referente por su dimensión deportiva y humana: "La Junta Directiva del Real Madrid C. F., reunida hoy miércoles 4 de noviembre, ha acordado someter a la Asamblea General de Socios Compromisarios la ratificación del nombramiento de Rafael Nadal Parera, socio número 67.778 de nuestro club, como nuevo miembro de la Junta Directiva. Rafael Nadal, socio de honor del Real Madrid, es una de las más grandes leyendas de la historia del deporte y uno de los deportistas españoles más admirados y reconocidos en todo el mundo. Para el Real Madrid y para todo el madridismo constituye un enorme orgullo que una figura de su dimensión deportiva y humana, un referente del deporte español y mundial, pase a formar parte de nuestra Junta Directiva y contribuya, desde esta responsabilidad, al presente y al futuro de nuestro club. Con su extraordinario palmarés, con 92 títulos individuales, entre ellos 22 Grand Slam, 2 medallas de oro olímpicas, 5 Copas Davis con España y el número 1 del ranking mundial, Rafael Nadal ha protagonizado una trayectoria deportiva legendaria. Pero su figura representa mucho más que sus éxitos: su talento, su espíritu de superación permanente, su capacidad de sacrificio, su competitividad, su humildad, su respeto a los rivales y a sus compañeros, y su compromiso solidario hacen de él un ejemplo dentro y fuera de las pistas. Todos estos valores forman parte de la identidad del Real Madrid y Rafael Nadal los ha representado y defendido a lo largo de toda su vida deportiva, convirtiéndose en un referente para millones de personas en todo el mundo". Rafa Nadal, a través de sus redes sociales, dio las gracias por la propuesta y comunicó que la había aceptado: "Quiero agradecer al presidente Florentino Pérez y a la Junta que me hayan propuesto entrar como parte de la Junta Directiva del Real Madrid. He aceptado esta propuesta con mucha ilusión, ganas de aprender y aportar todo lo que pueda".

articles.title: 10 Former College Football Players Who Would Have Broken the Bank With NIL
articles.summary: The NIL era has given student-athletes the opportunity to benefit financially from the juggernaut that is college athletics. But not long ago, even the smallest endorsement deal was prohibited.
articles.body:
The NIL era has given student-athletes the opportunity to benefit financially from the juggernaut that is college athletics. But not long ago, even the smallest endorsement deal was prohibited.

Looking back through college football history, some memorable stars would have cleaned up in today's NIL landscape based on a combination of their on-field success, the market they played in and their personality.

Deion Sanders is a perfect example of a player who was ahead of his time in building his personal brand. Tim Tebow later spent four seasons at the University of Florida as one of the most recognizable athletes in all of sports.

Here, we've highlighted 10 former college football stars who would be millionaires before starting their pro careers if they were still on campus today.

Brian Bosworth was decades ahead of his time when it came to cultivating a personal brand.

A fearsome presence in the middle of Oklahoma coach Barry Switzer's defense, he remains the only player who won the Butkus Award for college football's best linebacker twice. He was also a cultural phenomenon thanks to his signature bleached-blonde mullet, bad-boy persona and crushing hits on the field.

Bosworth was barred from playing in the 1987 Orange Bowl after testing positive for steroids. Switzer dismissed him from the team days after he appeared on the sidelines wearing a T-shirt that referred to the NCAA as "National Communists Against Athletes."

That didn't stop the Seattle Seahawks from taking him No. 1 overall in the 1987 NFL supplemental draft. He signed a then-record 10-year, $11 million rookie deal , although shoulder issues cut his NFL career short.

An All-American cornerback and standout punt returner, Deion Sanders also had a larger-than-life personality dating back to his days at Florida State.

Beyond his All-American play on the gridiron, he also started for the FSU baseball team and was on the track team. He famously played a doubleheader and ran a leg on the relay team on the same day.

Sanders brought a level of showmanship and swagger to college football that was not as commonplace at the time, and he consistently backed it up with his shutdown ability on defense and dynamic impact in the return game.

His "Prime Time" persona was well-established during his college days, and he carried it into his pro career, showing up to the NFL combine in a limo before reportedly running a 4.27-second 40-yard dash.

There might not be a player featured here better built for the NIL era than the man who's now coaching at the University of Colorado.

The numbers don't tell the full story of just how significant Michael Vick's redshirt freshman season was at Virginia Tech in 1999.

He had 1,840 passing yards, 585 rushing yards and 20 total touchdowns, but he was more than just a dual-threat quarterback. His elite 180.4 passer rating and 12.1 yards per attempt were a newfound level of impact from a passer built to scramble.

Vick led the Hokies to an 11-0 regular season and a Sugar Bowl meeting with Florida State for the national championship, but they ultimately lost to quarterback Chris Weinke and the Seminoles.

However, he returned for another season in 2000, and no one was more exciting in college football during his two-year run before he went No. 1 overall in the 2001 NFL draft to the Atlanta Falcons.

Much like the Fab Five at Michigan revolutionized college basketball in the 1990s, Vick's performance and success helped usher in an era of dual-threat quarterbacks. His constant presence on highlight reels made him a marketing dream, too.

Legendary HS Coach Freddie Gibbs Dies at 89

Could USC have put together the NIL deals needed to keep both Reggie Bush and Matt Leinart on the roster in 2005?

Both had just finished in the top five in Heisman Trophy balloting for a team that went 13-0, with Leinart taking home the hardware, and they returned to chase a third national championship.

That proven production, combined with their Hollywood market, made them the faces of college football during their time on campus. Bush's ability to dominate the SportsCenter highlight reel puts him front and center.

He had 1,740 rushing yards and 478 receiving yards during the 2005 season, and he also returned kicks and punts on his way to 19 total touchdowns. He would have been the first choice for national marketing campaigns.

Multiple players do it each year in today's game, but Vince Young was just the eighth quarterback in college football history with 1,500 passing yards and 1,000 rushing yards in the same season in 2004.

His 59.2 percent completion rate and 12 touchdowns against 11 interceptions left him out of the top-tier quarterback conversation entering his junior season at the University of Texas, but his unique dual-threat talents had just led the Longhorns to an 11-1 season.

All of that would have made him an NIL dream entering what would be an epic junior year where he had 3,036 passing yards, 1,050 rushing yards and 38 total touchdowns on his way to leading Texas to a national championship over USC's vaunted roster.

He would have been battling for the spotlight with Reggie Bush and Matt Leinart, but in one of college football's most memorable seasons, there would have been plenty of attention to go around.

The wholesome image that defined Tim Tebow throughout his four-year run at the University of Florida would have attracted an entirely different set of NIL sponsors than those drawn to some of the other players on this list.

After filling a supporting role on Florida's 2006 championship team, he spent three years as one of the most impactful players in the history of college football, starting with his 2007 Heisman Trophy season when he had 32 passing touchdowns, 23 rushing touchdowns and 4,181 total yards.

Tebow remains the only player to play two full collegiate seasons after winning the Heisman Trophy, which helped make him a household name by the time his four-year run at Florida ended.

It's hard to imagine a player having more NIL opportunities than Tebow would have over the course of his collegiate career, especially considering the impact he made as a freshman before ever taking over the starting job.

Another player who was ahead of his time when it came to building a personal brand, Tyrann Mathieu was a do-it-all defensive back who became a household name thanks to his "Honey Badger" nickname.

With 76 tackles, six forced fumbles, five fumble recoveries, two interceptions and 1.5 sacks during the 2011 season, he filled up the stat sheet and served as the defensive centerpiece for an LSU defense that allowed just 11.3 points per game and played in the BCS championship game.

Mathieu finished fifth in Heisman Trophy voting that season and fully embraced his nickname, which was rooted in a viral video about the actual animal. He even incorporated it into his look, dyeing the top of his hair blonde.

His college career ended before the 2012 season when LSU dismissed him following repeated violations of its substance-abuse policy, according to ESPN . In today's NIL era, it's worth considering whether those violations would have carried the same consequences for his college career.

The first freshman in history to win the Heisman Trophy, Johnny Manziel racked up 3,706 passing yards, 1,410 rushing yards and 47 total touchdowns in 2012 while leading a Texas A&M team that went 7-6 the year before to an 11-2 record.

Adding to the storyline of his historic freshman season was Texas A&M coach Kevin Sumlin's strict policy of not letting freshmen speak to the media, which cultivated an air of mystery around the phenom.

While Manziel came out of nowhere for his record-setting freshman season, he was undeniably the face of college football at the start of his sophomore campaign. His NIL price tag would have been astronomical in today's game.

Manziel later said he earned at least $33,000 signing autographs at Texas A&M in 2013. With NIL opportunities, his earning potential could have been far greater.

Even during his days at Florida State, Jameis Winston had the personality to match his arm talent. Making him the de facto face of college football would have been a no-brainer for NIL purposes.

He threw for 4,057 yards and 40 touchdowns to win the Heisman Trophy and lead Florida State to a national championship as a redshirt freshman in 2013, which established him as the top passer in the country heading into the 2014 campaign.

In April 2014, Winston received a civil citation following an incident involving unpaid seafood at a grocery store and subsequently completed community service. He later said a store employee had given him the seafood, an account Publix said its investigation did not corroborate.

In today's NIL landscape, a player of Winston's stature could earn thousands of dollars through endorsements—opportunities unavailable to college athletes at the time.

After attempting just 39 passes across two seasons at Ohio State, Joe Burrow transferred to LSU in 2018 and replaced Danny Etling as the team's starting quarterback.

Burrow threw for 2,894 yards and 16 touchdowns in his first season in Baton Rouge for an LSU squad that leaned heavily on the running game and finished 10-3.

There undoubtedly would have been NIL opportunities for a returning SEC starting quarterback heading into the 2019 season, but his marketability exploded as his senior year unfolded.

Burrow finished with 5,671 passing yards and 60 touchdowns throwing to Justin Jefferson and Ja'Marr Chase while leading LSU to a perfect 15-0 record and a national championship. His looks and personality would have made him the most marketable player in the country during the 2019 campaign.
